ambiguities.ambiguity: The title says authoritative map, while the body says navigation/canonicalization only, does not override plan detail, and records routing only. The precedence rule when an index statement conflicts with an owner document is not explicit.
A governance seal may refresh artifacts after Plans and indexes stabilize, but may, stabilize, the deciding actor, and whether a seal is required are undefined.
Change Summary entries are not chronological: July 7 precedes July 5 and July 6 entries, July 9 precedes another July 7 entry, and no supersession ordering is declared.

The July 6 storage entry says provider stream, GUI, security, behavioral, and currentness blockers are not closed, while the following entry says the non-executable lane closes the spec/schema/validator/fixture scope for corresponding categories. The index does not identify stable closure IDs or an explicit layered-status relation that prevents broad misreading.

The web schema is called the shared owner for numerous shapes and many product documents are consumers, but no document is identified as the behavioral SSOT for WebOperation lifecycle, browser execution, research policy, or card behavior.
The owner-map guard sometimes assigns multiple primary owners to one seam without field-level authority partitions or precedence, despite stating that primary owners carry canon.
The separate seams with usage carry-through and without usage carry-through have no predicate specifying which operations, fields, or states select either branch.
Mixed-era layering is prohibited, but mixed-era, additive patch, older framing, detection criteria, and the required retirement transformation are not defined here.

Owner decision and official stable releases are invoked for exact toolchain versions without naming the owner record or defining whether a newly released version automatically invalidates the pinned target.

claims.claim: The file presents itself as an authoritative Plans map, asserts compliance with DRY, Contracts_V0, packaging, and deterministic-decision policy, but limits its operative authority to navigation, canonicalization, and owner routing rather than re-owning detailed behavior.
Assistant memory and GitHub integration are registered in the canonical map, with assistant-memory-subsystem identified as the Assistant-only memory SSOT.

Planning-ledger, Plan Document System, plan-to-node boundary, Goal Runtime, Orchestrator Goal Runtime Flow, and semantic-audit closure authority are registered; generated governance refresh is deferred to an explicit seal after live Plans and permitted PlanUnit indexes stabilize.

Plans-to-code handoff and bootstrap compilation remain design/Plans/index-only and are prohibited from creating or dispatching WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, GoalRuns, runtime dispatch, implementation files, generated governance artifacts, or production build tasks in the enumerated lanes.

PRD/Planning runtime contract artifacts cover named service, snapshot, stage, node, activation, testing, UICommand, clean-room, and retired-search contracts; their validator is part of standard gates. Chain-wizard documents and CW/CWF PlanUnits are retired to compatibility/source-lineage status and may not be accepted as active truth.

Provider routing retires Gemini CLI, retains API-key-backed Gemini Direct, substitutes Antigravity CLI for the CLI-backed Google/agent route, requires provider-to-model catalogs, distinguishes media route directions, requires both subscription-backed and official API-key OpenAI image routes, and makes readiness route/model/account-specific.
PM History, native vision_bridge/see_image, and Teach/Teacher are registered while PMConcept.html remains non-final source lineage; that compile is explicitly non-executable and non-sealing.

Docker/Hosts is specified as a native Slint routed page/lab entered from Docker Manager and cross-surface links; docker_manager owns the Activity Bar panel and command namespace, Coasts is source-lineage only, and runtime families are whole-MVP but capability-probed and gated.

PMConcept control reconciliation and production wiring/exclusion artifacts are registered, while PMConcept remains concept/source-lineage rather than canonical implementation markup, styling, or demo state.

The active GUI/toolchain target is Rust stable 1.96.1 with Slint 1.17.1; native Winit/Skia is default, FemtoVG-wgpu is fallback, software is emergency fallback, and the first-build web GUI is a Slint/WASM canvas mediated by a trusted local daemon for OS-owned capabilities. Implementers must reverify official stable releases before build work.

Implementation-readiness artifacts and their generator/validator own the buildability gate. Approve And Build remains disabled whenever blockers are open or node readiness reports the hard-disabled PNC-019 boundary; plan artifacts, schemas, wiring, semantic closure, reports, or passing validators alone are insufficient proof of buildability.

Executor_Protocol solely owns execution_unit_context, its schema identity/version are fixed, and six named consumers reference it. This registration explicitly leaves EventRecord, storage values, provider stream, lifecycle, clean-room, GUI, and security blockers open and authorizes no executable output.

Contracts_V0 owns the persisted pm.event.v0 envelope, the JSON Schema materializes it, and storage-plan owns seglog/redb persistence, replay, retention, migration, legacy compatibility, and payload registration. Closure is expressly limited to the envelope and storage-value boundary.

The storage registry inventories storage-value families and materializes named launch-critical values; its schema owns registry shape, and the readiness script validates parsing, ownership, version, no-secret fields, and continued false buildability. Listed noncritical families are deferred_not_build_blocking with owner, reason, and reopen condition.

Non-executable closure evidence claims closure only for the spec/schema/validator/fixture layer across nine categories; runtime lifecycle and clean-room harness remain open, PNC-019 remains hard-disabled, buildability remains false, and no executable/product artifacts are created.

The web-operation schema is registered as shared shape authority for web operations, jobs, research, citations, browser state/results, adapters, and UI cards. No-secret seed/projection, source receipt, positive/negative fixtures, and finding-coverage artifacts are registered; generated-governance refresh and live projection synchronization remain separate lanes, and the registration itself creates no runtime or build output.

Models_System owns active model capability limits, fallback chains, provenance, and requested/effective capability fields; Contracts_V0 owns only the cross-surface snapshot-reference envelope, named consumers depend on those owners, and platform_specs authority is retired.

Orchestrator canon-collapse has a required ten-document reading order followed by seven primary consumer documents; owner documents must be reconciled before consumers, stale-era alternatives may not survive as peers, and summaries/checklists follow owner and primary-consumer reconciliation.

The owner-map guard declares that primary-owner entries carry canon while adjacent, cross-owner, stale-consumer, and implicated documents are reconciliation companions. It enumerates contract, storage, UI, run-graph, usage, HITL, executor, runtime-artifact, and mixed-era seams.

cross_window_seams.seam: The Cross-doc owner-map guard heading starts at line 67, while its operative authority rule and seam inventory continue through the permitted overlap and beyond this core. The next window must preserve the routing-only limitation and determine whether unique field-level owners are ultimately supplied.
Provider, PM History/vision/Teach, and Docker/Hosts registrations require exact owner-document destinations and consumer propagation outside this window.
Governance sealing, readiness generation, blocker state, PNC-019, and non-executable closure evidence require generation/currentness/atomicity behavior in their owning artifacts and scripts.

The web schema and fixture family propagates to Tools, contracts, storage, evidence, commands, chat/GUI, prompt, run-mode, Goal, persona, PRD, wizard, MCP, model, permission, and testing consumers; behavioral ownership and parity must be verified across those consumers.

Model capability authority is split between Models_System and a Contracts_V0 reference envelope, with assistant chat and OpenCode as consumers; later windows must preserve that field-level split and legacy exclusion.

The mandatory reading/reconciliation order flows into the owner-map seam inventory; later windows must define or route the reconciliation oracle, stale-canon detection, and multi-owner conflict precedence.

negative_space_observations.observation: Several entries advertised as owner routing name capabilities and source ledgers but do not identify an exact active owner-document path, so the index provides claims without a deterministic authority destination.

The build gate states when Approve And Build is disabled but does not state behavior for missing, stale, malformed, partially regenerated, mutually inconsistent, unavailable, or concurrently changing blocker/readiness reports, nor identify override authority or fail-open/fail-closed semantics.

Release reverification is mandatory but has no named actor, authoritative source set, cadence, freshness threshold, persisted receipt, mismatch transition, compatibility policy, or oracle for deciding whether implementation may proceed.

The trusted local daemon boundary is asserted without identity, authentication, authorization, consent, origin binding, secret handling, revocation, audit, offline, compromise, or malicious-input behavior in this routing entry.

Governance sealing, generated gate reports, evidence generation, and live provider projection synchronization are referenced without atomicity, idempotency, interruption/resume, stale-output rejection, or concurrent-writer rules in this window.

Provider readiness and web fixtures mention denied, partial, fallback, timeout, unavailable, and security cases, but the index does not route a complete state machine covering empty, unknown, estimated, stale, cancelled, resumed, offline, overload, malicious, or recovery behavior to a named behavioral owner.

GUI-facing claims identify pages, controls, disabled build state, render fallbacks, and web cards but contain no routing or oracle for truthful state presentation, keyboard/screen-reader accessibility, localization, responsive behavior, focus, reduced motion, truncation, or error recovery.

No performance, capacity, backpressure, latency, resource-budget, telemetry, support, or operational-response contract is attached to the provider, daemon, storage, build-gate, or web-operation claims in this window.

Named validators and fixtures establish artifact-level test surfaces, but the window does not map each behavioral claim to a positive/negative executable oracle or state that all consumers must pass the same oracle.
The required reading and reconciliation order has no named caller, trigger, enforcement mechanism, failure response, persisted completion state, or definition of successful reconciliation.
